text:
maria: eu-central1 NVMe p99 jumped to ~400ms, GPU attach backlog increasing. anyone oncall?

sre-bot: ALERT: pool=eu-central1-local read_p99=402ms; attach_failures rising.

alex: quick scan shows a fleet-wide rekey/re-encrypt job started after yesterday's KMS rotation. many fscrypt workers scanning /scratch.

jamal: that coupled with scheduled cleanup jobs would explain the small-read storm. can we stop re-encrypts safely?

kevin: key-ops triggered it automatically. it's safe to pause; re-encrypt isn't urgent. I'll pause the rollout.

maria: mitigation plan: 1) pause key-ops rollout (kevin) 2) apply per-node IO caps to fscrypt workers 3) route new gpu attaches away from eu-central1 for short window.

alex: commands I used on a node to cap the process (example):
```bash
# create cgroup v2 bucket and apply io cap
mkdir -p /sys/fs/cgroup/rekey
echo "8:0 rbps=40M r_iops=300 wbps=80M w_iops=500" > /sys/fs/cgroup/rekey/io.max
# move pid 4129 into group
echo 4129 > /sys/fs/cgroup/rekey/cgroup.procs
```

kevin: rollout paused. signalled in-flight jobs to exit gracefully. routing pref set to us-west2 for 20m.

sre-bot: ACTION: key-ops paused (kevin); in-flight rekey workers signalled (maria); routing pref updated: us-west2 for 20m.

jamal: after caps p99 sampled nodes back to ~30ms and attach retries successful. follow-ups: add IO-headroom preflight in key-ops, stagger re-encrypts, and include quick rollback play in runbook.

maria: filing INFRA-9001: "rekey-triggered NVMe IO surge -> headroom interlock + per-job IO caps" with playbook and cost estimate for regional routing. monitoring eu-central1 now. :white_check_mark:
